ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, in $\triangle ABC$, AE is the altitude on side BC. If AD is the bisector of $\angle BAC$, $\angle B=40^\circ$, and $\angle C=50^\circ$, what is the measure of $\angle DAE$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution}:\\
Since $\angle B=40^\circ$ and $\angle C=50^\circ$,\\
it follows that $\angle BAC=90^\circ$,\\
Since $AD$ is the bisector of $\angle BAC$,\\
it results in $\angle BAD=45^\circ$,\\
Since $\angle ADE$ is an exterior angle of $\triangle ABD$,\\
it follows that $\angle ADE=\angle B+\angle BAD=40^\circ+45^\circ=85^\circ$,\\
Therefore, $\angle DAE=90^\circ-85^\circ=\boxed{5^\circ}$.

Reasoning: It is known that ∠B=40° and ∠C=50°, so the sum of the interior angles of the triangle gives ∠BAC=180°−40°−50°=90°. AD is the angle bisector of ∠BAC, therefore ∠BAD=45°. Because E is on BC, ∠ABE=∠ABC=40°; and because AE is perpendicular to BC, ∠AEB=90°. In right triangle ABE, ∠BAE=180°−90°−40°=50°. In the figure AD is located between AB and AE, so ∠DAE=∠BAE−∠BAD=50°−45°=5°.
